method: WebSearch only (WebFetch blocked). Every 'quote' is the fragment the search result showed, not text read on the page itself. No number here was computed by the researcher; ratios are recorded only where the source states them. Vendor blogs carry a commercial interest and are graded low.

topics.noEvidence: No laminate maker (Rogers, Isola, Panasonic) or independent index publishes a price or ratio; no Panasonic R-1566 figure found; Sierra Circuits publishes none (only an unanswered forum question). topics.toolUsesToday: Rogers / PTFE laminate is NOT priced (F14, docs/pcb/pcb-pipeline-fixes-2026-10-09.md §4); the 'Rogers 4350B: 8–12×' figure appears only in the rf_microwave prompt text (server/routes/pcb.ts:1174, F15 - prompt guidance, no price). On automotive_adas boards an 'automotive laminate' premium = fabCost × 0.40 × (0.35, or 0.50 at ≥8 layers), i.e. 14% / 20% of fab (server/routes/pcb.ts:947-948), plus an IATF fab premium of 18% (server/routes/pcb.ts:946); both unsourced engineering figures.

topics.topic: 5. OEM / Tier-1 contract price versus distributor list price for semiconductors at automotive volume

claims.claim: Distributor online price usually reflects the manufacturer's suggested price; the distributor pays a 'book' cost and the online price reflects its margin
claims.context: Altium Resources, how component prices are set
claims.quote: In almost all cases this price reflects the suggested price published by the manufacturer. In reality the distributor is paying a set cost to the manufacturer (the "book" cost)

claims.claim: Manufacturers may 'break' the distributor's book cost on high-volume sales; illustrative example halves a $2.00 book cost
claims.context: Cadence PCB resources, 2019, illustrative example not market data
claims.quote: the manufacturer would debit back to the distributer a portion of their cost reducing the book price from $2.00 to $1.00

claims.claim: Avnet (franchised distributor) consolidated gross margin FY2025 10.7% (FY2024 11.6%) - the distributor's whole-business margin, not a contract-price gap
claims.context: Avnet Form 10-K FY2025 (year to 28 June 2025)
claims.quote: [paraphrase in search summary, no verbatim fragment] Margin fell to 10.7%, from 11.6% a year earlier.

claims.claim: TechInsights' component price landscape blends contract OEM pricing with algorithmic estimates at target volume, 2x and 0.5x (no discount curve published)
claims.context: TechInsights subscription description
claims.quote: determine market pricing for your BOM at projected target volume, twice the projected target volume and half the projected target volume

claims.claim: Rule of thumb: a BOM cost above 80% of the lowest online price suggests overpaying
claims.context: Pricing-software vendor heuristic, not analyst data
claims.quote: if your BOM cost is over 80% of the lowest online price, you're likely overpaying

topics.noEvidence: No analyst or industry statement with a figure for how far automotive OEM / Tier-1 contract prices sit below distributor 1k / reel prices was found (TechInsights, S&P/IHS, Yole SystemPlus sell the data but publish no discount; Caresoft / Munro nothing). The only numeric comparisons are illustrative (Cadence) or a vendor heuristic (Cofactr).
topics.toolUsesToday: Catalogue lines are priced at distributor breaks along a franchise curve (10k = 1k × 0.85, b = 0.0706), DERIVED above the largest published break and flat above 300k parts (server/utils/pcb-price-catalogue.ts:17-25, :153+); class/named tables are read as ~10k reel prices (TABLE_BASIS_QTY, server/routes/pcb.ts:55-56). No contract-price discount below distributor pricing is applied, except imagers, which take an 'automotive volume' class rule (£3-15) instead of a listing (server/utils/pcb-bom-grounding.ts:22-26).
